title: The book I read
goal: Describe a thing by what someone did with it, with the participle and a possessive ending on the noun.

intro.text: When the noun is the thing done, its possessive ending says who did it: *okan kitabym*, the book I read (literally my read book). The genitive pronoun is optional: *(meniň) okan kitabym*. With `-ýAn`: *işleýän ýerim*, the place where I work.

vocab.en: ring (ýüzügi: the ring, as an object)
favourite (iň gowy görýän aýdymym: my favourite song)

exercises.question: How do you say **the book I read**?

why.1: *Okanym kitap* says **what I read is a book**. The possessive goes on the noun: *okan kitabym*.
why.2: Without the possessive, nothing says who read it: *okan kitabym*.
why.3: The participle comes before the noun: *okan kitabym*.

exercises.en: I've read the book you gave me.

accept: yňy

reject.why: *-ym* is **my**. You gave it: *seniň beren kitabyňy*.
Say whose giving it was: *seniň beren kitabyňy*.

accept: The book I read yesterday is very interesting.
The book that I read yesterday is very interesting.
The book I read yesterday was very interesting.
The book that I read yesterday was very interesting.

exercises.prompt: Where is the ring you gave me?
accept: Seniň maňa beren ýüzügiň nirede?

exercises.explain: *maňa beren ýüzük* with **your**: *ýüzügiň*; k becomes g before the vowel.

why.2: The possessive says who does the action there: I work there.
